title: Water Equivalent (W) — Definition & Derivation
notes: **Definition:** the mass of water that would absorb or release the same amount of heat (H) as a given object, for the same temperature change (Δθ)
**For the equivalent mass of water:** H = W·c_w·Δθ
Since H and Δθ are identical in both cases: m·c·Δθ = W·c_w·Δθ → cancelling Δθ gives **W = (m·c)/c_w**
**Note:** in the CGS system, c_w = 1 cal/g°C, so W is numerically equal to m·c
